summary_paragraph: A man with end-stage renal disease, type II diabetes, Chagas-related cardiomyopathy, and a history of coronary artery bypass grafting was admitted for evaluation of fever and found to have a worsening pleural effusion. He had recently undergone a failed AV fistula attempt and presented with malaise, chills, and cough. Workup included thoracentesis and pleuroscopic biopsy, which showed exudative fluid with active pleuritis but no malignancy or infection. He underwent thoracoscopy and pleurodesis to prevent reaccumulation. Post-procedure, he developed bradycardia and hyperkalemia, likely vagally mediated, which resolved with insulin therapy and hemodialysis. His fever resolved, attributed to a viral syndrome. He was discharged home with a PleurX catheter for outpatient drainage, visiting nurse support, and follow-up appointments.
